rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa reads lāqū rather than laqū; both forms mean meeting someone nearby face to face.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حنيفة رحمه الله و إذا لاقوا يقال لقيته ولاقيته إذا استقبلته قريبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites feign friendly faces and claim belief when meeting believers while mocking them.
rows.anchor: في بيان ما كانوا يعملون مع المؤمنين من الاستهزاء بهم ولقائهم بوجوه المصادقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khala ilayhi means being alone with someone; ilayhi marks both departure from believers and arrival among their leaders.
rows.anchor: خلوت بفلان وإليه إذا انفردت معه وبالى أبلغ لأن فيه دلالة الإبتداء والإنتهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their satanic leaders are rebellious people like devils, identified either as Jewish leaders or as anyone resembling devils in rebellion.
rows.anchor: وشياطينهم الذين ماثلوا الشياطين في تمردهم وهم اليهود

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh says the nūn in shayāṭīn is original, citing the verb tashayṭana.
rows.anchor: وعن سيبويه أن نون الشياطين أصلية بدليل قولهم تشيطن

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh also gives the alternative that shayāṭīn derives from shatana, to be distant from right conduct and truth.
rows.anchor: وعنه أنها زائدة واشتقاقه من شطن إذا بعد لبعده من الصلاح والخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further derivation connects the word to shāṭa, meaning to perish; al-bāṭil is among its names.
rows.anchor: أو من شاط إذا بطل ومن أسمائه الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell the believers they are companions and agree with them, then tell their own leaders with emphatic certainty that they remain with them.
rows.anchor: إنا مصاحبوكم وموافقوكم على دينكم و إنما خاطبوا المؤمنين بالجملة الفعلية وشياطينهم بالإسمية محققة بأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim to believers is unconvincing because their convictions do not motivate it and emphasis would not persuade people surrounded by the Emigrants and Helpers.
rows.anchor: لأن انفسهم لا تساعدهم عليه إذ ليس لهم من عقائدهم باعث ومحرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among their own faction, affirmation suits their desire and is accepted, so it is emphatic.
rows.anchor: فقد كان عن رغبة وقد كان متقبلا منهم رائجا عنهم فكان مظنة للتحقيق ومئنة للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that they only mock Islam confirms their loyalty to Judaism and rejects Islam, since mockery treats its object as invalid.
rows.anchor: تأكيد لقوله إنا معكم لأن معناه الثبات على اليهودية وقوله إنما نحن مستهزئون رد للاسلام ودفع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement can also be a fresh reply to an objection: if you are with us, why agree with the believers? They answer that they are only mocking.
rows.anchor: أو استئناف كأنهم اعترضوا عليهم بقولهم حين قالوا لهم إنا معكم إن كنتم معنا فلم توافقون المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istihzāʾ means mockery and contempt; its root connotes lightness, from a word for rapid killing.
rows.anchor: والاستهزاء السخرية والاستخفاف وأصل الباب الخفة من الهزء وهو القتل السريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They exchanged guidance for misguidance, choosing error in its place.
rows.anchor: أى استبدلوها به واختاروها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies people who believed and later disbelieved; another identifies Jews who believed in Muḥammad and then rejected him.
rows.anchor: لأنها فى قوم آمنوا ثم كفروا أو فى اليهود الذين كانوا مؤمنين بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما جاءهم كفروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, guidance was so available to them that it is depicted as already established within them before they left it for error.
rows.anchor: أو جعلوا لتمكنهم منه كأن الهدى قائم فيهم فتركوه بالضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trade metaphor supports the validity of a sale by mutual action without spoken offer and acceptance, when one takes an item and leaves its agreed price.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على جواز البيع تعاطيا لأنهم لم يتلفظوا بلفظ الشرا ولكن تركوا الهدى بالضلالة عن اختيارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalāla is deviation from the intended path or loss of guidance, metaphorically applied to religious error.
rows.anchor: والضلالة الجور عن القصد وفقد الاهتداء يقال ضل منزله فاستعير للذهاب عن الصواب فى الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing profit to trade is figurative; extending the buying metaphor with profit and trade is rhetorical reinforcement, illustrated by a poem extending its raven-and-eagle comparison with nests.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الربح إلى التجارة من الإسناد المجازي ومعناه فما ربحوا فى تجارتهم إذ التجارة لا تربح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their being unguided means they do not know profitable and loss-making commercial routes; their capital was guidance, which they lost for error.
rows.anchor: لطرق التجارة كما يكون التجار المتصرفون العالمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trader seeks preservation of capital and profit, but they lost both; worldly gains cannot count as profit when guidance is gone.
rows.anchor: أن مطلوب التجار سلامة رأس المال والربح وهؤلاء قد أضاعوهما فرأس مالهم الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A grammatical alternative makes all of الذين a modifier of أولئك and the rest of the verse its predicate.
rows.anchor: وقيل الذين صفة أولئك وفما ربحت تجارتهم إلى آخر الآية فى محل الرفع خبر أولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The breakers of God's covenant may be obstinate Jewish scholars, their hypocrites, or disbelievers generally.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهؤلاء الناقضين لعهد الله احبار اليهود المتعنتون أو منافقوهم أو الكفار جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant may be the rational evidence for God's oneness implanted in human minds, treated as a binding charge.
rows.anchor: ما ركز فى عقولهم من الحجة على التوحيد كأنه أمر وصاهم به ووثقه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may be the pledge to affirm and follow a messenger whom God supports with miracles, rather than conceal his description.
rows.anchor: بأنهم إذا بعث إليهم رسول يصدقه الله بمعجزاته صدقوه واتبعوه ولم يكتموا ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is a pledge not to shed one another's blood, oppress one another, or sever kinship.
rows.anchor: أن لا يسفكوا دماءهم ولا يبغى بعضهم على بعض ولا يقطعوا أرحامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A threefold account distinguishes the primordial covenant with Adam's descendants, the prophets' duty to convey revelation, and scholars' duty to disclose scripture.
rows.anchor: عهد الله إلى خلقه ثلاثة عهود العهد الأول الذي أخذه على جميع ذرية آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mīthāq derives from firmness; its pronoun refers to the covenant they undertook to keep, or describes God's binding it upon them.
rows.anchor: أصله من الوثاقة وهى إحكام الشئ والضمير للعهد وهو ما وثقوا به عهد الله من قبوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they sever means either kinship and alliance with believers or the connection among prophets who agree on truth, which they break by selective belief.
rows.anchor: هو قطعهم الأرحام وموالاة المؤمنين أو قطعهم ما بين الانيباء من الوصلة والاجتماع على الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about what God ordered joined has grammatical alternatives: ما is indefinite described by the following clause or a relative pronoun, with أن nominally attached in two ways.
rows.anchor: وما نكرة موصوفة أو بمعنى الذى و أن يوصل فى موضع جر بدل من الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption in the land includes blocking roads and obstructing faith.
rows.anchor: بقطع السبيل والتعويق عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are the losers: the emphatic pronoun separates the subject, and they are deceived and deprived.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أولئك ﴾ مبتدأ ﴿ هم ﴾ فصل والخبر ﴿ الخاسرون ﴾ أى المغبونون حيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their loss is exchanging breach for fidelity, severance for connection, corruption for reform, and punishment for reward.
rows.anchor: استبدلوا النقض بالوفاء والقطع بالوصل والفساد بالصلاح والعقاب بالثواب

rows.speaker: مدني
rows.claim: The Medinan reading has أوصى instead of وصى.
rows.anchor: وأوصى مدنى وشامى

rows.speaker: شامي
rows.claim: The Syrian reading likewise has أوصى instead of وصى.
rows.anchor: وأوصى مدنى وشامى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun بها refers either to the religious community or to the declaration أسلمت لرب العالمين.
rows.anchor: بالملة أو بالكلمة وهى أسلمت لرب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb is coordinated with Abraham and therefore also commanded his sons to keep this religion.
rows.anchor: هو معطوف على إبراهيم داخل فى حكمه والمعنى ووصى بها يعقوب بنيه أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God selected Islam as the finest religion and enabled them to adopt it.
rows.anchor: أعطاكم الدين الذى هو صفوة الأديان وهو دين الإسلام ووفقكم للأخذ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is not to die except while steadfast in Islam; it forbids being in another state at death, as a command not to pray except humbly forbids lack of humility.
rows.anchor: الإسلام إذا ماتوا كقولك لا تصل إلا و أنت خاشع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the disconnected reading, the question denies that the believers witnessed Jacob's death; they know it only through revelation.
rows.anchor: أو منقطعة ومعنى الهمزة فيها الإنكار والشهداء جمع شهيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the connected question addresses Jews who claimed every prophet died a Jew, challenging whether they witnessed Jacob's death.
rows.anchor: أو متصلة ويقدر قبلها محذوف والخطاب لليهود لأنهم كانوا يقولون ما مات نبى إلا على اليهودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second إذ either apposes the first or serves as an adverb for شهداء or حضر.
rows.anchor: يدل من إذ الأولى والعامل فيهما شهداء أو ظرف لحضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob asks generally what his sons worship after his death; ما may ask what thing or what attribute of the deity, like asking whether Zayd is a jurist or doctor.
rows.anchor: ما استفهام فى محل النصب بتعبدون أى أى شيء تعبدون وما عام فى كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They answer that they worship the God of their forefathers; Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are appositional clarifications of forefathers.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان لآبائك وجعل إسماعيل من جملة آبائه وهو عمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismāʿīl is included among Jacob's fathers because an uncle counts as a father; a report calls al-ʿAbbās the remainder of my fathers.
rows.anchor: وجعل إسماعيل من جملة آبائه وهو عمه لأن العم اب قال عليه السلام فى العباس هذا بقية آبائى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilāhan wāḥidan is either an appositive to the preceding deity or an accusative of specification meaning they intend one God.
rows.anchor: بدل من إله آبائك كقوله بالناصية ناصية كاذبة أو نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We are Muslims is either a circumstantial clause, coordinated with worship, or parenthetical emphasis.
rows.anchor: حال من فاعل نعبد أو جملة معطوفة على نعبد أو جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They exchanged guidance for misguidance and forgiveness for punishment by concealing the description of Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: يكتمان نعت محمد عليه السلام ﴿ فما أصبرهم على النار ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما أصبرهم is a reproachful question: what makes them endure doing deeds that lead to the Fire?
rows.anchor: فأى شيء أصبرهم على عمل يؤدى إلى النار وهذا استفهام معناه التوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They went out to fight Goliath and his troops, asking God to pour patience on them in battle and help them against the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: خرجوا لقتالهم ﴿ قالوا ربنا أفرغ ﴾ أصبب ﴿ علينا صبرا ﴾ على القتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firm steps mean strengthening their hearts and casting terror into the enemy's hearts.
rows.anchor: بتقوية قلوبنا والقاء الرعب فى صدور عدونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadāyantum means dealing with one another by debt, whether one lends or borrows.
rows.anchor: أى إذا داين بعضكم بعضا يقال داينت الرجل إذا عاملته بدين معطيا أو آخذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A specified term is a known period, such as harvest, threshing, or the pilgrims' return.
rows.anchor: مدة معلومة كالحصاد أو الدياس أو رجوع الحاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning debt supplies the antecedent for فاكتبوه and clarifies deferred versus immediate debt; the phrasing is more elegant than repeating الدين.
rows.anchor: احتيج إلى ذكر الدين ولم يقل إذا تداينتم إلى اجل مسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing a deferred debt is recommended because it better guards against forgetfulness and denial.
rows.anchor: أمر بكتابة الدين لأن ذلك أوثق وآمن من النسيان وأبعد من الجحود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this concerns salam; after forbidding usury, God permitted a guaranteed advance sale for a known term and revealed the longest verse, requiring a term for salam.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما أن المراد به السلم وقال لما حرم الله الربا أباح السلف المضمون إلى أجل معلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scribe must be trustworthy and precise, adding nothing and omitting nothing; the debtor's document should be legally valid.
rows.anchor: كاتب مأمون على ما يكتب يكتب بالاحتياط لا يزيد على ما يجب أن يكتب ولا ينقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scribe should understand legal conditions, so the parties should select a learned, upright jurist who writes only what Islamic law accepts.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل أن يكون الكاتب فقيها عالما بالشروط حتى يجئ مكتوبه معدلا بالشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No scribe should refuse to write the document as God taught, altering or changing its form.
rows.anchor: كتابة الوثائق لا يبدل ولا يغير وكما متعلق بأن يكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor, as the person liable and subject to testimony, must dictate, making the document his verbal admission; إملال and إملاء are synonymous forms.
rows.anchor: إلا من وجب عليه الحق لأنه هو المشهود على ثباته فى ذمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor must fear God, neither refusing to dictate in denial of the debt nor understating any part of it.
rows.anchor: الذى عليه الدين ربه فلا يمتنع عن الإملاء فيكون جحودا لكل حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safīh may mean mentally impaired or legally restrained for wastefulness and poor judgment; ḍaʿīf means a child; inability includes stammering, muteness, or not knowing the language.
rows.anchor: أى مجنونا لأن السفه خفة فى العقل أو محجورا عليه لتبذيره وجهله بالتصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the debtor cannot dictate, the guardian who manages his affairs dictates truthfully and justly.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فليملل وليه ﴾ الذى يلى امره ويقوم به ﴿ بالعدل ﴾ بالصدق والحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two witnesses are sought from believing men; Islam, freedom, and adulthood are conditions, while the author's school accepts non-Muslims testifying among themselves.
rows.anchor: من رجال المؤمنين والحرية والبلوغ شرط مع الإسلام وشهادة الكفار بعضهم على بعض مقبولة عندنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If two men are unavailable, one man and two women may witness; male testimony with women is accepted outside fixed punishments and retaliation.
rows.anchor: فليشهد رجل وامرأتان وشهادة الرجال مع النساء تقبل فيما عدا الحدود والقصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witnesses should be people whose uprightness is known; this implies some witnesses are not approved.
rows.anchor: ممن تعرفون عدالتهم وفيه دليل على أن غير المرضى شاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two-witness clause explains that one woman may forget the testimony and the other remind her; Ḥamza reads the verb with nominative and gemination under the conditional, while Makki and Baṣri read it accusatively from dhikr.
rows.anchor: إن تضل إحداهما على الشرط فتذكر بالرفع والتشديد حمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses are called witnesses before they testify because the anticipated event is treated as already actual; the first command is obligatory in principle and the second recommended.
rows.anchor: وسماهم شهداء قبل التحمل تنزيلا لما يشارف منزلة الكائن فالأول للفرض والثاني للندب

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poet uses s-simt to express becoming weary with life after eighty years, supporting the sense of ولا تسأموا as do not tire.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر سئمت تكاليف الحياة ومن يعش ثمانين حولا لا أبا لك يسأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in أن تكتبوه may refer to the debt or the document; small or large can describe the debt's value, supporting salam in textiles, or describe a concise or detailed record.
rows.anchor: والضمير فى ﴿ أن تكتبوه ﴾ للدين أو الحق ﴿ صغيرا أو كبيرا ﴾ على أى حال كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Write the debt through its agreed due date; ذلك refers to the act of writing as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: إلى وقته الذى اتفق الغريمان على تسميته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing is more equitable before God, better supports testimony, and reduces doubt about amount and qualities by providing a written reference.
rows.anchor: أقرب من انتفاء الريب للشاهد والحاكم وصاحب الحق فإنه قد يقع الشك فى المقدار والصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparative forms أقسط and أقوم follow Sībawayh's derivation from the causative verbs اقسط and أقام.
rows.anchor: وبنى أفعلا التفضيل أى أقسط وأقوم من اقسط وأقام على مذهب سيبويه

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads the phrase so تجارة is the noun of كان or an appositional clarification of trade.
rows.anchor: عاصم أى إلا أن تكون التجارة تجارة أو إلا أن تكون المعاملة تجارة حاضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings analyze يكون as complete, meaning an immediate transaction occurs, or as incomplete with تجارة حاضرة as its subject and تديرونها as predicate.
rows.anchor: غيره تجارة حاضرة على كان التامة أى إلا أن تقع تجارة حاضرة أو هى ناقصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Managing a spot trade means exchanging it hand to hand; there is no harm in leaving it unwritten because no debt-related suspicion arises.
rows.anchor: معنى إدارتها بينهم تعاطيها يدا بيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing sales is recommended for immediate and deferred exchanges as a precaution, or the command concerns immediate trade alone, where testimony suffices without writing.
rows.anchor: أمر بالإشهاد على التبايع مطلقا ناجزا أو كالئا لأنه أحوط وأبعد من وقوع الإختلاف

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki reads تذكرة with accusative from dhikr rather than the other derivation.
rows.anchor: فتذكر بالنصب مكى وبصرى من الذكر لا من الذكر

rows.speaker: بصري
rows.claim: Baṣri shares the accusative reading تذكرة from dhikr.
rows.anchor: فتذكر بالنصب مكى وبصرى من الذكر لا من الذكر

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar reads يضارر in the active voice; Ibn ʿAbbās reads يضار in the passive.
rows.anchor: يحتمل البناء للفاعل لقراءة عمر رضى الله عنه ولا يضارر وللمفعول لقراءة ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ولا يضار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the passive form ولا يضار, while ʿUmar's active form is ولا يضارر.
rows.anchor: لقراءة عمر رضى الله عنه ولا يضارر وللمفعول لقراءة ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ولا يضار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active reading forbids a scribe or witness to refuse, distort, add, or omit; the passive forbids burdening them, rushing them from duties, withholding the scribe's fee, or making a witness bear travel costs.
rows.anchor: النهى عن الضرار بهما بأن يعجلا عن مهم ويلزا أولا يعطى الكاتب حقه من الجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Causing such harm is sinful conduct; fear God in this duty, and God teaches the laws of religion without forgetfulness or deficiency.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإن تفعلوا ﴾ و إن تضاروا ﴿ فإنه ﴾ فان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harming the scribe or witnesses is sinful conduct; fear God in this duty.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فسوق بكم ﴾ مأثم ﴿ واتقوا الله ﴾ فى مخالفة أ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God teaches the laws of religion and knows everything without forgetfulness or deficiency.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويعلمكم الله ﴾ شرائع دينه ﴿ والله بكل شيء عليم ﴾ لا يلحقه سهو ولا قصور

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki reads رهٰن as رهان; both readings are plurals of رهن, first a verbal noun later declined as a noun.
rows.anchor: فرهان مكى و أبو عمرو أى فالذى يستوثق به رهن وكلاهما جمع رهن

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr shares the reading رهان, with رهٰن as another plural of رهن.
rows.anchor: فرهان مكى و أبو عمرو أى فالذى يستوثق به رهن وكلاهما جمع رهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel creates the likelihood that writing and witnesses are unavailable, so collateral is guidance for preserving property in their place.
rows.anchor: ولما كان السفر مظنة لا عواز الكتب والاشهاد أمر على سبيل الإرشاد إلى حفظ المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word مقبوضة makes possession a condition for a valid pledge; this rejects Mālik's view that offer and acceptance alone suffice.
rows.anchor: اشتراط القبض لا كما زعم مالك أن الرهن يصح بالإيجاب والقبول بدون القبض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the creditor trusts the debtor, no writing, witnesses, or pledge is needed; the debtor must repay the entrusted debt and not deny it.
rows.anchor: فإن أمن بعض الدائنين بعض المديونين بحسن ظنه به فلم يتوثق بالكتابة والشهود والرهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the debt an amanah reflects the lender's trust in leaving it unpledged even though the debt remains guaranteed.
rows.anchor: وسمى الدين أمانة وهو مضمون لإئتمانه عليه بترك الارتهان منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to conceal testimony addresses witnesses.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا تكتموا الشهادة ﴾ هذا خطاب للشهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase إثم قلبه may make the heart the agent of sin or make it the subject of a fronted predicate; attribution to the heart emphasizes that concealment is inwardly hidden.
rows.anchor: ارتفع قلبه بآثم على الفاعلية كأنه قيل فإنه يأثم قلبه أو بالابتداء وآثم خبر مقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart is named because concealment begins inside it; deeds attributed to their organ are more emphatic, and the heart leads the body, so the sin occupies the self's noblest place.
rows.anchor: لأن كتمان الشهادة أن يضمرها فى القلب ولا يتكلم بها فلما كان إثما مقترفا مكتسبا بالقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making this a sin of the heart marks it among the gravest sins, since faith and disbelief, the basis of good and evil, are also acts of the heart.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أن أصل الحسنات والسيآت الإيمان والكفر وهما من أفعال القلوب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās names associating partners with God, false testimony, and concealing testimony among the greatest major sins.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما أكبر الكبائر الإشراك بالله وشهادة الزور وكتمان الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows whether testimony is concealed or disclosed, and nothing is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والله بما تعملون ﴾ من كتمان الشهادة وإظهارها ﴿ عليم ﴾ لا يخفى عليه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must be patient in religion and its duties.
rows.anchor: على الدين وتكاليفه قال الجنيد رضى الله عنه الصبر

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Al-Junayd defines patience as restraining oneself from what is disliked without agitation.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد رضى الله عنه الصبر حبس النفس على المكروه بنفى الجزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compete with God's enemies in jihad by enduring war's hardships, showing no less patience or steadfastness than they do.
rows.anchor: أعداء الله فى الجهاد أى غالبوهم فى الصبر على شدائد الحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maintain posts at the frontier, keeping horses there while watchful and ready to fight.
rows.anchor: وأقيموا فى الثغور رابطين خيلكم فيها مترصدين مستعدين للغزو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falah is remaining with what one loves after escaping hardship; laʿalla keeps the outcome uncertain so believers do not rely on hopes without doing good first.
rows.anchor: الفلاح البقاء مع المحبوب بعد الخلاص عن المكروه ولعل لتغيب المآل لئلا يتكلوا على الآمال عن تقديم الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A spiritual interpretation reads the commands as patience in God's love, perseverance amid His favors, and tethering the self in His service to attain closeness.
rows.anchor: وقيل اصبروا فى محبتى وصابروا فى نعمتى ورابطوا أنفسكم فى خدمتى

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the two radiant chapters, al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān, will come on Judgment Day as clouds or flocks of birds, pleading for their companions.
rows.anchor: قال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرؤوا الزهراوين البقرة وسورة آل عمران فانهما يأتيان يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Test orphans' understanding and ability to manage property before puberty by letting them handle it; this supports a discerning child's permission to trade.
rows.anchor: واختبروا عقولهم وذوقوا أحوالهم ومعرفتهم بالتصرف قبل البلوغ فالابتلاء عندنا أن يدفع إليه ما يتصرف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching marriage means puberty, when a person becomes fit for marriage and its purpose of procreation.
rows.anchor: أى الحلم لأنه يصلح للنكاح عند ولطلب ما هو مقصود به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anīsū means they have discerned sound judgment in handling business and transactions.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فإن آنستم منهم ﴾ تبينتم ﴿ رشدا ﴾ هداية فى التصرفات وصلاحا فى المعاملات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once puberty and discernible judgment are present, deliver their property without delay; the syntax makes release conditional on judgment after puberty.
rows.anchor: من غير تأخير عن حد البلوغ ونظم هذا الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite رشد either specifies commercial judgment or signals that even a little sound judgment suffices; this supports Abū Ḥanīfa's release of property at age twenty-five.
rows.anchor: وتنكير الرشد يفيد أن المراد رشد مخصوص وهو الرشد فى التصرف والتجارة أو يفيد التقليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not consume the property wastefully or rush to spend it before the orphans grow up and reclaim it; the verbal nouns are circumstantial or purposive.
rows.anchor: ولا تأكلوها مسرفين ومبادرين كبرهم فاسرافا وبدارا مصدران فى موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rich guardian must refrain from the orphan's property; a poor guardian may take a carefully measured customary amount.
rows.anchor: قسم الأمر بين أن يكون الوصى غنيا وبين أن يكون فقيرا فالغنى يستعفف

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm defines a poor guardian's customary share as enough to fill hunger and cover nakedness.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم ما سد الجوعة ووارى العورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When returning the property, obtain witnesses to prove receipt and avoid denial or a disputed oath.
rows.anchor: بأنهم تسلموها وقبضوها دفعا للتجاحد وتفاديا عن توجه اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥasīb means one who audits and reckons; alternatively, it warns the guardian taking a customary share not to exceed it because God will account for it.
rows.anchor: محاسبا فعليكم بالتصادق وإياكم والكاذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meeting God can mean reaching the afterlife and what follows, or can be taken literally, since denying resurrection also denies vision of God.
rows.anchor: ببلوغ الآخرة وما يتصل بها أو هو مجرى على ظاهره لأن منكر البعث منكر للرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The endpoint particle reaches the coming of the Hour, not their loss, which has no end.
rows.anchor: ﴿ حتى ﴾ غاية لكذبوا لا لخسر لأن خسرانهم لا غاية له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour is the Resurrection; its delayed arrival followed by eternity makes its intervening duration like one hour.
rows.anchor: أى القيامة لأن مدة تأخرها مع تأبد ما بعدها كساعة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghtatan means suddenly and may be parsed as a circumstantial accusative or cognate accusative, the hour arriving without warning of its time.
rows.anchor: فجأة وانتصابها على الحال يعنى باغتة أو على المصدر كأنه قيل بغتتهم الساعة بغتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclamation personifies regret, calling it to come because its time has arrived.
rows.anchor: نداء تفجع معناه يا حسرة احضرى فهذا أوانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They regret neglecting either worldly life or the Hour itself by failing to prepare for or believe in it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ على ما فرطنا ﴾ قصرنا ﴿ فيها ﴾ فى الحياة الدنيا أو فى الساعة أى قصرنا فى شأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sins on their backs uses the familiar image of carrying heavy things; it figuratively means sin clings to them without leaving.
rows.anchor: خص الظهر لأن المعهود حمل الأثقال على الظهور كما عهد الكسب بالأيدى وهو مجاز عن اللزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report depicts the dead person's ugly deed as a foul-smelling figure: it says the person rode it in life, and now it rides him.
rows.anchor: وقيل أن الكافر إذا خرج من قبره استقبله أقبح شيء صورة وأخبثه ريحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle ألا intensifies the severity of what is said next.
rows.anchor: وأفاد ألا تعظيم ما يذكر بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's people argued against God's oneness and denied partners to Him.
rows.anchor: فى توحيد الله تعالى ونفى الشركاء عنه

rows.speaker: مدني
rows.claim: The Medinan reading has اتحاجونى for the question about disputing Abraham over God.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال أتحاجوني في الله ﴾ فى توحيده اتحاجونى مدنى وابن ذكوان

rows.speaker: ابن ذكوان
rows.claim: Ibn Dhakwān shares the reading اتحاجونى.
rows.anchor: والياء فى الوصل أبو عمرو ولما خوفوه أن معبوداتهم

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr retains the yāʾ in وقد هدان when pausing or connecting the reading.
rows.anchor: والياء فى الوصل أبو عمرو ولما خوفوه أن معبوداتهم تصيبه بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says he never fears their idols, which have no power to benefit or harm; only God could choose to make something harmful or beneficial.
rows.anchor: لا أخاف معبوداتكم فى وقت قط لانها لا تقدر على منفعة ولا مضرة إلا إذا شاء ربى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows everything, so no harm or benefit reaches anyone except by His knowledge.
rows.anchor: فلا يصيب عبدا شيء من ضر أو نفع إلا بعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering should lead them to distinguish the powerful God from powerless idols.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أفلا تتذكرون ﴾ فتميزوا بين القادر والعاجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's people fear powerless idols yet do not fear associating with God a partner for whom He gave no proof; they misplace security and fear.
rows.anchor: حجة إذ الاشراك لا يصح أن يكون عليه حجة والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two groups are monotheists and polytheists; Abraham asks which deserves safety from punishment.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فأي الفريقين ﴾ أى فريقى الموحدين والمشركين ﴿ أحق بالأمن ﴾ من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says which group rather than which of us to avoid praising himself.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل فأينا احترازا من تزكية نفسه

rows.speaker: الصديق
rows.claim: Here ظلم means associating partners with God, according to al-Ṣiddīq; such believers receive security and guidance.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم ﴾ بشرك عن الصديق رضى الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call addresses people who prohibited crops and livestock; تعالوا originally invited someone below from a higher place before becoming a general invitation.
rows.anchor: هو من الخاص الذى صار عام وأصله أن يقوله من كان فى مكان عال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ألا تشركوا explains what is recited, rather than supplying a prohibition particle.
rows.anchor: أى مفسرة لفعل التلاوة ولا للنهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindness to parents appears among prohibitions because requiring kindness necessarily forbids neglecting it; the same applies to the following commands.
rows.anchor: ولما كان إيجاب الإحسان تحريما لترك الإحسان ذكر فى المحرمات وكذا حكم ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not kill children from poverty or fear of poverty; God provides for parents and children because He sustains His servants.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق ﴾ من أجل فقر ومن خشيته كقوله خشية إملاق ﴿ نحن نرزقكم وإياهم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Public indecencies concern conduct between people, private ones what is between a person and God; the public phrase apposes الفواحش.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها ﴾ ما بينك وبين الخلق ﴿ وما بطن ﴾ ما بينك وبين الله ما ظهر بدل من الفواحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A protected life may be taken only by right, such as retaliation, execution for apostasy, or stoning.
rows.anchor: كالقصاص والقتل على الردة والرجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These detailed commands are what God charged people to preserve, so they may recognize their seriousness before Him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ذلكم وصاكم به ﴾ أى المذكور مفصلا أمركم ربكم بحفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best way to approach an orphan's property is to protect and grow it.
rows.anchor: إلا بالخصلة التى هى أحسن وهي حفظه وتثميره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching full strength means attaining puberty; then the property is delivered. Shadd is a singular form like fals.
rows.anchor: مبلغ حلمه فادفعوه إليه وواحده شد كفلس وأفلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fair measure and weight means equality and justice; the following capacity limit excuses unavoidable difficulty in observing the precise margin.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأوفوا الكيل والميزان بالقسط ﴾ بالسوية والعدل ﴿ لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God requires only what a person can bear; anything beyond the attainable measure is excused because exact limits may be burdensome.
rows.anchor: وإنما اتبع الأمر بإيفاء الكيل والميزان ذلك لأن مراعاة الحد من القسط الذى لا زيادة ولا نقصان مما فيه حرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When speaking or judging, be truthful and just even where a relative is concerned, whether in testimony or otherwise.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا ﴾ فأصدقوا ﴿ ولو كان ذا قربى ﴾ ولو كان المقوم له أو عليه فى شهادة أو غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's covenant may be the primordial covenant or His commands, prohibitions, promise and threat, vows, and oaths; all are to be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: يوم الميثاق أو فى الأمر والنهى والوعد والوعيد والنذر واليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza, ʿAlī, and Ḥafṣ read the form with one tāʾ omitted; others geminate it through assimilation, meaning take heed.
rows.anchor: بالتخفيف حيث كان حمزة وعلى وحفص على حذف إحدى التاءين

rows.speaker: شامي
rows.claim: The Syrian reading lightens أن, from أنه with an omitted pronoun; this makes the straight path a reason for following it.
rows.anchor: و لأن هذا صراطى فهو علة للاتباع بتقدير اللام و أن بالتخفيف شامى

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads إن as a new sentence at its beginning.
rows.anchor: أن بالتخفيف شامى وأصله و أنه على أن الهاء ضمير الشأن والحديث

rows.speaker: على
rows.claim: ʿAlī also reads إن as a new sentence.
rows.anchor: ﴿ مستقيما ﴾ حال ﴿ فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل ﴾ الطرق المختلفة فى الدين من اليهودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path is straight, and the commands to follow it and avoid diverging religious paths apply to Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, innovations, and error.
rows.anchor: الطرق المختلفة فى الدين من اليهودية والنصرانية والمجوسية

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet drew one straight line as God's path, then six slanting lines on each side, each with a devil calling to it, and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: روى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خط خطا مستويا ثم قال هذا سبيل الرشد وصراط الله فاتبعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Splitting each of the twelve paths into six yields seventy-two divergent routes away from Islam.
rows.anchor: ثم يصير كل واحد من الأثنى عشر طريقا ستة طرق فتكون اثنين وسبعين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these decisive verses in all the scriptures have never been abrogated.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما هذه الآيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says these verses were the first thing in the Torah.
rows.anchor: وعن كعب أن هذه الآيات لأول شيء فى التوارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence from understanding to remembering and then God-consciousness reflects reasoning, taking heed, and avoiding forbidden acts.
rows.anchor: ذكر اولا تعقلون ثم تذكرون ثم تتقون لأنهم إذا عقلوا تفكروا ثم تذكروا أى اتعظوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting hands and feet crosswise means taking one limb from each side; Pharaoh was the first to use this punishment and crucify its victims.
rows.anchor: هو أول من قطع من خلاف وصلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The only supposed fault Pharaoh can find in them is faith, which is actually the source of honor and distinction; the poet similarly calls sword-wear the sole blemish of warriors.
rows.anchor: وما تعيب منا إلا ما هو أصل المناقب والمفاخر وهو الإيمان ومنه قوله ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer asks for wide, abundant patience, as if it were poured over and flooded them.
rows.anchor: أى اصبب صبا ذريعا والمعنى هب لنا صبرا واسعا واكثره علينا حتى يفيض علنا ويغمرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask to die as Muslims, meaning steadfast in Islam.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وتوفنا مسلمين ﴾ ثابتين على الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional has an omitted verb governing أحد, understood as if it said: if someone from the polytheists seeks protection after the treaty months, grant it so he can hear monotheism and Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: أحد مرتفع بفعل شرط مضمر يفسره الظاهر أى وان استجارك أحد استجارك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He remains protected until he hears and reflects on God's word and understands the truth.
rows.anchor: ﴿ حتى يسمع كلام الله ﴾ ويتدبره ويطلع على حقيقة الامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If he does not convert, escort him back to safety before fighting him if desired; a protected visitor must not be harmed or kept from returning, and may not settle in Muslim territory.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ثم أبلغه ﴾ بعد ذلك ﴿ مأمنه ﴾ داره التى يأمن فيها إن لم يسلم ثم قاتله إن شئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protection is given because they are ignorant of Islam and need security to hear and understand its truth.
rows.anchor: بسبب أنهم قوم جهلة لا يعلمون ما الإسلام وما حقيقة ما تدعوا إليه فلا بد من اعطائهم الأمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides from heaven through rain and from earth through vegetation.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قل من يرزقكم من السماء ﴾ بالمطر ﴿ والأرض ﴾ بالنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone creates and forms hearing and sight in their astonishing detail, or protects their delicate organs from injury over time.
rows.anchor: من يستطيع خلقهما وتسويتهما على الحد الذى سويا عليه من القطرة العجيبة أو من يحميها من الآفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living can mean animals, chicks, crops, believers, and scholars from fluids, eggs, and seeds, and their opposites.
rows.anchor: أي الحيوان والفرخ والزرع والمؤمن والعالم من النطفة والبيضة والحب والكافر والجاهل وعكسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Management of the whole world follows the particular examples, widening the argument from specific divine powers to universal governance.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن يدبر الأمر ﴾ ومن يلى تدبير أمر العالم كله جاء بالعموم بعد الخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since they acknowledge God as the only one able to do these things, they should abandon associating partners with Him in worship.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فسيقولون الله ﴾ فسيجيبونك عند سؤالك أن القادر على هذه هو الله ﴿ فقل أفلا تتقون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God with such power is the true Lord, whose lordship is certain to anyone who reasons carefully.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فذلكم الله ﴾ أى من هذه قدرته هو الله ﴿ ربكم الحق ﴾ الثابت ربوبيته ثباتا لا ريب فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no middle ground between truth and error; whoever leaves truth falls into error.
rows.anchor: أى لا واسطة بين الحق والضلال فمن تخطى الحق وقع في الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are being turned away from truth to error and from monotheism to idolatry.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فأنى تصرفون ﴾ عن الحق إلى الضلال وعن التوحيد إلى الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lose themselves by exchanging worship of God for worship of idols.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم ﴾ حيث اشتروا عبادة الآلهة بعبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fabricated gods and supposed intercessors disappear, leaving them with nothing they had imagined.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وضل عنهم ﴾ وبطل عنهم وضاع ما اشتروه وهو ﴿ ما كانوا يفترون ﴾ من الآلهة وشفاعتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are the greatest losers in the afterlife because they led others astray and turned away themselves.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون ﴾ بالصد والصدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis takes لا as rejecting a preceding claim, جرم as acquired, and the whole as saying their claim earns them loss in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أن لا رد لكلام سابق أى ليس الامر كما زعموا ومعنى جرم كسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis treats لا جرم as a compound meaning truly, with their loss as the subject of what is true.
rows.anchor: أن لا جرم كلمتان ركبتا فصار معناهما حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis understands the expression to mean inevitably.
rows.anchor: وثالثها أن معناه لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They come at night to conceal the truth and embolden themselves to make an excuse.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وجاؤوا أباهم عشاء ﴾ للاستتار والتجسر على الاعتذار

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash says no one should believe a person who cries after Joseph's brothers.
rows.anchor: حال عن الأعمش لا تصدق باكية بعد إخوة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing their cries, Jacob is alarmed and asks if something happened to their flock, then asks what happened and where Joseph is.
rows.anchor: فلما سمع صوتهم فزع وقال مالكم با بنى هل أصابكم فى غنمكم شيء قالوا لا قال فما بالكم وأين يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nastabiqū may mean racing on foot or competing in archery; the derived forms iftiʿāl and tafāʿul can overlap, as in throwing/competing to throw.
rows.anchor: أى نتسابق العدو أو فى الرمى والافتعال والتفاعل يشتركان كالارتماء والترامى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say Jacob will not believe their story even if they speak truth, because he loves Joseph intensely and distrusts the brothers.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولو كنا صادقين ﴾ ولو كنا عندك من أهل الصدق والثقة لشدة محبتك ليوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blood described as كذب either means blood connected with a lie or uses a verbal noun as an intensified adjective, as when a liar is called falsehood itself.
rows.anchor: ذى كذب أو وصف بالمصدر مبالغة كأنه نفس الكذب ويعنه كما يقال للكذاب هو الكذب بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says they slaughtered a lamb, stained Joseph's shirt with its blood, and forgot to tear it.
rows.anchor: روى أنهم ذبحوا سخلة ولطخواالقميص بدمها وزل عنهم أن يمزقوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report has Jacob demand the shirt, cast it over his face, and cry until the shirt's blood stained his face; he remarks that no wolf was ever so gentle as to eat his son without tearing the shirt.
rows.anchor: وأخذه وألقاه على وجهه وبكى حتى خضب وجهه بدم القميص وقال تالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shirt had three signs: it proved the brothers lied, restored Jacob's sight when placed on his face, and showed Joseph's innocence because it was torn from behind.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان فى قميص يوسف ثلاث آيات كان دليلا ليعقوب على كذبهم وألقاه على وجهه فارتد بصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase على قميصه is an adverbial expression meaning the blood was over the shirt.
rows.anchor: ومحل على قميصه النصب على الظرف كأنه قيل وجاءوا فوق قميصه بدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says their selves made an immense deed seem attractive or easy to them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بل سولت ﴾ زينت أوسهلت ﴿ لكم أنفسكم أمرا ﴾ عظيما ارتكبتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣabr jamīl can be parsed as a predicate or a subject with an omitted predicate; the most beautiful patience is making no complaint to people.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فصبر جميل ﴾ خبر أو مبتدأ لكونه موصوفا أى فأمرى صبر جميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob seeks God's help in bearing what they claim about Joseph's death and the grief of his loss.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والله المستعان ﴾ أى أستعينه ﴿ على ﴾ احتمال ﴿ ما تصفون ﴾ من هلاك يوسف والصبر على الرزء فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min may be partitive, meaning God gave some of everything requested; alternatively, He gave all requested and unrequested things.
rows.anchor: من للتبعيض أي آتاكم بعض جميع ما سألتموه أو وآتاكم من كل شيء سألتموه وما لم تسألوه

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads ما سألتموه as a negation in a circumstantial clause: God granted all those things although people did not ask.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عمرو وما سألتموه نفى ومحله النصب على الحال أي آتاكم من جميع ذلك غير سائليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ما is relative: God gave what people needed as if they had asked or requested it implicitly.
rows.anchor: أو ما موصولة أي وآتاكم من كل ذلك ما احتجتم إليه فكأنكم سألتموه أو طلبتموه بلسان الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot count or reach the end of God's blessings, even if they count them generally; only God knows them in detail.
rows.anchor: لا تطيقوا عدها وبلوغ آخرها هذا إذا أرادوا أن يعدوها على الاجمال وأما التفصيل فلا يعلمه إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is unjust to a blessing by neglecting gratitude and intensely ungrateful; another reading is that hardship makes one complain while comfort makes one hoard and withhold.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن الإنسان لظلوم ﴾ يظلم النعمة باغفال شكرها ﴿ كفار ﴾ شديد الكفران لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān is generic, applying to anyone in whom injustice and ingratitude are found.
rows.anchor: والإنسان للجنس فيتناول الأخبار بالظلم والكفران من يوجدان منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children adorn worldly life but do not provide provisions for the grave or the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ﴿ المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا ﴾ لا زاد القبر وعدة العقبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enduring good works may be any good deed whose fruit remains for a person.
rows.anchor: أعمال الخير التي تبقى ثمرتها للانسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the enduring deeds are the five prayers.
rows.anchor: أو الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation lists glorifying God, praising Him, declaring His oneness, and magnifying Him.
rows.anchor: أو سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These works are better in reward and hope because God's promise is true whereas most worldly hopes are false; a person hopes for God's reward here and receives it in the next life.
rows.anchor: لأنه وعد صادق وأكثر الآمال كاذبة يعني أن صاحبها يأمل في الدنيا ثواب الله ويصيبه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' deeds are nullified and they will have no weight or worth before God on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أولئك الذين كفروا بآيات ربهم ولقائه فحبطت أعمالهم فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا ﴾ فلا يكون لهم عندنا وزن ومقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase may modify an omitted event or serve as the object of recall; tradition says Moses left with his family after asking Shuʿayb to visit his mother, during a dark snowy night after a birth, loss of the road and livestock, and failure to kindle fire; the apparent fire was light.
rows.anchor: روى أن موسى عليه السلام استأذن شعيبا في الخروج إلى أمه وخرج بأهله فولد له ابن في الطريق في ليلة مظلمة مثلجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amkuthū means remain in your place; ānastu means I saw, from perceiving something that offers comfort.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فقال لأهله امكثوا ﴾ اقيموا في مكانكم ﴿ إني آنست ﴾ ابصرت ﴿ نارا ﴾ والايناس رؤية شيء يؤنس به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses frames his hope cautiously so he does not promise what he has not yet confirmed.
rows.anchor: بني الأمر على الرجاء لئلا يعد ما ليس يستيقن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabas means an ember carried on a stick or a wick/tinder.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بقبس ﴾ نار مقتبس في رأس عود أو فتبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudā can mean a guide or people who guide him to the road; على marks the elevated place where people stand by the fire.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أو أجد على النار هدى ﴾ ذوي هدى أو قوما يهدونني الطريق ومعنى الاستعلاء في على النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse turns away from any thought that God takes amusement, declaring instead that His practice is to cast truth upon falsehood.
rows.anchor: بل اضراب عن اتخاذ اللهو وتنزيه منه لذاته كأنه قال سبحاننا أن نتخذ اللهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth may be the Qurʾān, Islam against idolatry, or earnestness against play; falsehood may mean Satan or idolatry.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بالحق ﴾ بالقرآن ﴿ على الباطل ﴾ الشيطان أو بالإسلام على ا لشرك أو بالجد على اللعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadmaghu means breaks and overcomes; falsehood then departs and perishes.
rows.anchor: فيكسره ويدحض الحق الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Casting and striking the head are a subtle bodily metaphor: strong truth strikes weak falsehood and makes it perish.
rows.anchor: وهذه استعارة لطيفة لأن أصل استعمال القذف والدمغ في الاجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse closes by condemning their attribution of a child and other claims to God.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولكم الويل مما تصفون ﴾ الله به من الولد ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After apostasy, the idol neither harms if left unserved nor benefits if worshipped; this is far error.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يدعو من دون الله ﴾ يعني الصنم فإنه بعد الردة يفعل كذلك ﴿ ما لا يضره ﴾ ان لم يعبده

none: The segment repeats the verse's words without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complete the measure and do not deprive people of their rights: full measure is commanded, short measure forbidden, and excess is unaddressed and therefore commendable if given but not required.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أوفوا الكيل ﴾ أتموه ﴿ ولا تكونوا من المخسرين ﴾ ولا تنقصوا الناس حقوقهم فالكيل واف

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says Moses completed the longer term and married the younger daughter, contrary to the narrative reported earlier.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام قضى اوفاهما وتزوج صغراهما وهذا بخلاف الرواية التي مرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses traveled with his wife toward Egypt after finishing the term.
rows.anchor: بامرأته نحو مصر قال ابن عطاء لما أتم أجل المحنة ودنا أيام الزلفة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ reads the completed ordeal and journey as nearing intimacy with God and the light of prophethood, so Moses' family shares in subtle divine acts.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء لما أتم أجل المحنة ودنا أيام الزلفة وظهرت أنوار النبوة سار باهله ليشتركوا معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He saw fire at Mount Sinai and asked his family to wait while he sought directions because they had lost the road, or a burning brand to warm themselves.
rows.anchor: ﴿ آنس من جانب الطور نارا قال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر ﴾ عن الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul experiences death's bitterness and distress as one tastes food; certainty of death makes leaving one's homeland easier.
rows.anchor: أى واجدة مرارته وكربه كما يجد الذائق طعم المذوق لأنها إذا تيقنت بالموت سهل عليها مفاوقة وطنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After death people return to God for reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ثم إلينا ترجعون ﴾ بعد الموت للثوب والعقاب

rows.speaker: يحيى
rows.claim: Yaḥyā reads يرجعون in the passive.
rows.anchor: يرجعون يحيى ترجعون يقعوب

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads ترجعون in the active address form.
rows.anchor: يرجعون يحيى ترجعون يقعوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will settle believers in lofty chambers of Paradise; the wording means lodging them there to stay.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنبوئنهم من الجنة غرفا ﴾ لننزلهم من الجنة علالى

rows.speaker: كوفي
rows.claim: The Kufans except ʿĀṣim read a form from thawā, meaning to stay, rather than the majority reading from lodging them.
rows.anchor: لبثوينهم كوفى غير عاصم من الثواء وهو النزول للاقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is made to take both believers and chambers either by analogy with lodging them, deleting a preposition, or construing the locative as an object.
rows.anchor: والوجه في تعديته إلى ضمير المؤمنين وإلى الغرف أما أجراؤه مجرى لننزلنهم لنؤوينهم أو حذف الجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text notes a pause at العاملين depending on the following syntactic analysis, but the excerpt breaks off before completing it.
rows.anchor: ويوقف على العاملين على أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذين صبروا may predicate an omitted subject, listing patience in leaving home, facing polytheists, trials, calamities, obedience, and avoiding sins.
rows.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف أى هم الذين صبروا على مفارقة الأوطان وعلى أذى المشركين وعلى المحن والمصائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Connecting الذين to the previous verse as a modifier of العاملين is better than starting a new clause.
rows.anchor: والوَصل أجود ليكون الذين نعتا للعاملين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They rely on God alone through all these hardships.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وعلى ربهم يتوكلون ﴾ ولم يتوكلوا فى جميع ذلك إلا على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be patient with their harm and hostility; God's promised victory over enemies and the triumph of Islam over every religion must come to pass.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فاصبر ﴾ على أذاهم أو عداوتهم ﴿ إن وعد الله ﴾ بنصرتك على أعدائك وإظهار دين الإسلام على كل دين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not let unbelievers rush you into asking for their punishment, or agitate and distress you through what they say and do; their doubt makes such behavior unsurprising.
rows.anchor: لا يحملنك هؤلاء الذين لا يوقنون بالآخرة على الخفة والعجلة فى الدعاء عليهم بالعذاب أو لا يحملنك على الخفة والقلق

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the final nūn with sukūn in ولا يستخفنك.
rows.anchor: ولا يستخفنك بسكون النون عن يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اذكر إذ means remember when Luqmān admonished his son.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإذ ﴾ أى واذكر إذ ﴿ قال لقمان لابنه ﴾ أنعم أو اشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase beginning أنعم أو اشكر is given as another wording or interpretation in the exhortation to his son.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال لقمان لابنه ﴾ أنعم أو اشكر

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki reads yā bunayya with sukūn.
rows.anchor: الاسكان مكى يا بنى حفض بفتحه فى كل القرآن

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads yā bunayya with fatḥa throughout the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: يا بنى حفض بفتحه فى كل القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associating partners is great injustice because it equates the One who supplies every blessing with beings that provide none.
rows.anchor: لأنه تسوية بين من لا نعمة الا وهى منه ومن لا نعمة له أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother bears increasing weakness upon weakness as pregnancy grows heavier and her weakness compounds.
rows.anchor: أى حملته تهن وهنا على وهن أى تضعف ضعفا فوق ضعف أى يتزايد ضعفها ويتضاعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weaning is complete at the end of two years.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وفصاله في عامين ﴾ أى فطامة عن الرضاع لتمام عامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to thank God and parents explains the prior charge; the mother's long burden is an inserted reminder of her special right.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أن اشكر لي ولوالديك ﴾ هو تفسير لو صينا أى وصيناه بشكرنا وبشكر والديه

rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna says observing the five prayers thanks God, while praying for one's parents after each prayer thanks them.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عيينة من صلى الصلوات الخمس فقد شكر الله ومن دعا للوالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return is to God, who will hold each person accountable.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إلي المصير ﴾ أى مصيرك إلى وحسابك على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqmān's son should endure for God's sake when enjoining good and forbidding wrong, or endure afflictions, which bring gifts.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يا بني أقم الصلاة وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر واصبر على ما أصابك ﴾ فى ذات الله تعالى إذا أمرت بالمعروف ونهيت عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prescribed acts are among matters God has decisively made obligatory, as if cut off with a binding command; عزم is a verbal noun used for its object.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن ذلك ﴾ الذى وصيتك به ﴿ من عزم الأمور ﴾ أى مما عومه الله من الأمور أى قطعه قطع إيجاب وإلزام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These practices show that the same acts of worship were commanded among all nations.
rows.anchor: وهذا دليل على أن هذه الطاعات كانت مأمورا بها فى سائر الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust means obedience to God; its bearer is called treacherous until it is returned to its owner, like a burden of debt carried on someone.
rows.anchor: وهو يريد بالأمانة الطاعة لله ويحمل الأمانة الخيانة يقال فلان حامل للامانة ومحتمل لها أى لا يؤديها إلى صاحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vast heavens, earth, and mountains submit to God's will in the way fitting inanimate beings, obeying His creative acts and diverse arrangements.
rows.anchor: قد انقادت لأمر الله انقياد مثلها وهو ما يتأتى من الجمادات واطاعت له الطاعة التى تليق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also says the sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, and animals prostrate, and that some stones fall in awe.
rows.anchor: أن الشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال والشجر والدواب يسجدون لله وأن من الحجارة لما يهبط من خشية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike inanimate creation, humans can obey and submit as accountable rational beings; refusing the trust means betraying it rather than merely declining a physical burden.
rows.anchor: وأما الإنسان فلم تكن حاله فيما يصح منه من الطاعة ويليق به من الانقياد لأوامر الله ونواهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the heavens and mountains refused treachery, while humanity took on the trust by failing to discharge it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فأبين أن يحملنها ﴾ أى أبين الخيانة فيها وأن لا يؤدينها ﴿ وأشفقن منها ﴾ وخفن من الخيانة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is unjust by neglecting the trust and ignorant by missing its own good despite being able to fulfill it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنه كان ظلوما ﴾ لكونه تاركا لاداء الامانة ﴿ جهولا ﴾ لاخطائه ما يسعده مع تمكه منه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says unbelievers and hypocrites carried the trust by betraying it, but obedient prophets and believers cannot be called unjust and ignorant.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج الكافر والمنافق حملا الامانة أى خانا ولم يطيعا ومن أطاع من الأنبياء والمؤمنين فلا يقال كان ظلوما جهولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says the trust was so immense that the greatest created bodies refused it in awe, while weak humanity carried it and then betrayed its guarantee; the Arabic idiom compares this to fat being asked where it goes and answering that it straightens a crooked thing.
rows.anchor: وقيل معنى الآية أن ما كلفه الإنسان بلغ من عظمة أنه عرض على أعظم ما خلق الله من الاجرام

rows.speaker: الأكثر
rows.claim: Most readers omit the yāʾ in يا عباد.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قل يا عباد الذين آمنوا ﴾ بلا ياء عند الاكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God-consciousness means obeying His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.
rows.anchor: ﴿ اتقوا ربكم ﴾ بامتثال اوامره واجتناب نواهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who obey God in this life receive an indescribably good reward in the afterlife, entry into Paradise; في belongs to أحسنوا, not حسنة.
rows.anchor: أى أطاعوا الله فى الدنيا وفى يتعلق بأحسنوا لا بحسنة معناه الذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا فلهم حسنة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī attaches في to حسنة and interprets the good as health and well-being.
rows.anchor: وقد علقه السدى بحسنة ففسر الحسنة بالصحة والعافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's breadth removes any excuse for neglecting virtue at home: migrate to another land, following prophets and righteous people, and increase in good deeds and obedience.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأرض الله واسعة ﴾ أى لا عذر للمفرطين فى الاحسان ألبته حتى ان اعتلوا بأنهم لا يتمكنون فى أوطانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient endure leaving homes and kin, hardships, and trials for obedience and added good works; their reward exceeds calculation.
rows.anchor: على مفارقة أوطانهم وعشائرهم وعلى غيرها من تجرع الغصص واحتمال البلايا فى طاعة الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says their reward is beyond what a calculator can comprehend or know; this phrase is circumstantial description of the reward.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما لا يهتدى إليه حساب الحساب ولا يعرف وهو حال من الأجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When two good responses are possible, take the better one to repel an enemy's harm: answer insult with praise and return a good deed for a bad one.
rows.anchor: فخذ بالحسنة التي هى احسن من اختها اذا اعترضتك حسنتان فادفع بها السيئة التي ترد عليك من بعض اعدائك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such exceptional kindness can turn a hostile enemy into a close, affectionate friend.
rows.anchor: فإنك اذا فعلت ذلك انقلب عدوك المشاق مثل الولى الحميم مصافاة لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to repaying injury with kindness; only patient people, blessed with a great good fortune, can attain this quality.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وما يلقاها ﴾ اى وما يلقى هذه الخصلة التى هي مقابلة الاساءة بالاحسان ﴿ إلا الذين صبروا ﴾ الا اهل الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may answer an imagined question about how to act; alternatively, lā is emphatic, and the stronger comparative replaces the expected simple adjective to heighten the response.
rows.anchor: وانما لم يقل فادفع بالتي هي احسن لانه تقدير قائل قال فكيف اصنع فقيل ادفع بالتي هى احسن وقيل لا مزيدة للتأكيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the best response as patience in anger, forbearance amid ignorance, and pardon for injury; he interprets great fortune as reward.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما بالتي هى احسن الصبرعند الغضب والحلم عند الجهل والعفو عند الاساءة وفسر الحظ بالثواب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says no fortune is greater than Paradise.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن والله ما عظم حظ دون الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says the verse was revealed about Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb, an enemy who harmed the Prophet and later became a close friend.
rows.anchor: وقيل نزلت في ابى سفيان بن حرب وكان عدوا مؤذيا للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم فصار وليا مصافيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heedless are submerged in ignorance and inattentive to what they were commanded.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الذين هم في غمرة ﴾ في جهل يغمرهم ﴿ ساهون ﴾ غافلون عما امروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's people behave like earlier peoples who rejected messengers and called them sorcerers or madmen, out of ignorance.
rows.anchor: الامر مثل ذلك وذلك اشارة إلى تكذيبهم الرسول وتسميته ساحرا أو مجنونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every earlier messenger met the same accusation from his people.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ما أتى الذين من قبلهم ﴾ من قبل قومك ﴿ من رسول إلا قالوا ﴾ هو ﴿ ساحر أو مجنون ﴾ رموهم بالسحر أو الجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the accusation: did generations advise each other to repeat this identical charge?
rows.anchor: الضميرللفول اى اتواصى الاولون والاخرون بهذا القول حتى قالوه جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not coordinate because they lived at different times; the shared cause is transgression, which drives them to say it.
rows.anchor: لم يتواصوا به لانهم لم يتلاقوا في زمان واحد بل جمعتهم العلة الواحدة وهى الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the sky raised and supported, making it the source of His judgments and decrees and the abode of angels descending with revelation, a sign of His majesty and sovereignty.
rows.anchor: خلقها مرفوعة ومسموكة حيث جعلها منشأ احكامه ومصدر قضاياه ومسكن ملائكته الذين يهبطون بالوحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balance means every instrument for weighing and measuring, such as scales, a steelyard, a measure, or a gauge, placed on earth to govern fairness in people's exchanges.
rows.anchor: كل ما توزن به الاشياء وتعرف مقاديرها من ميزان وقرسطون ومكيال ومقياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Set measures fairly and do not diminish them; the first command forbids short measure and the second also forbids excessive deviation, while repeating الميزان strengthens the instruction.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ﴾ وقوموا وزنكم بالعدل ﴿ ولا تخسروا الميزان ﴾ ولا تنقصوه امر بالتسوية ونهى عن الطغيل الذى هو اعتداء وزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥāqqa is the Hour whose arrival is certain and unavoidable; the word derives from haqq, to be established or obligatory.
rows.anchor: الساعة الواجبة الوقوع الثابتة المجئ التي هي آتيه لا ريب فيها من حق بحق بالكسر أي وجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What could inform you of its nature? No creature can grasp the Hour's full greatness and severity; grammatically ما الحاقة begins a clause that serves as the second object of أدري.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وما أدراك ﴾ وأي شيء أعلمك ﴿ ما الحاقة ﴾ يعني أنك لا علم لك بكنهها ومدى عظمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān may mean Adam's offspring, or specifically Adam; in the latter view, the period is his time in the womb until he became known among people.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنا خلقنا الإنسان ﴾ أي ولد آدم وقيل الأول ولد آدم أيضا وحين من الدهر على هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amshāj is an adjective or apposition describing a drop mixed from two fluids; it is a singular word, not a plural, despite its form.
rows.anchor: ﴿ نطفة أمشاج ﴾ نعت أو بدل منها أي من نطفة قد امتزج فيها الماآن ومشجة ومزجة بمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabtali-hi is circumstantial: God created humanity intending to test it through commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: ﴿ نبتليه ﴾ حال أي خلقناه مبتلين أي مريدين ابتلاءه بالأمر والنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the human being hearing and seeing once these faculties came to be.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا ﴾ ا ذا سمع وبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed the path of guidance through rational proofs and revealed evidence.
rows.anchor: بينا له طريق الهدى بأدلة العقل والسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thankful means believing and ungrateful means disbelieving; these may be circumstantial descriptions of the person guided.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إما شاكرا ﴾ ا مؤمنا ﴿ وإما كفورا ﴾ كافرا حالان من الهاء في هديناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the path itself is figuratively described as a thankful path or an ungrateful path.
rows.anchor: أو من السبيل أي عرفناه السبيل اما سبيلا شاكرا واما سبيلا كفورا ووصف السبيل بالشكر والكفر مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After naming the two groups, the text follows with what God prepared for each.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر الفريقين اتبعهما ما اعد لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Woe is the predicate for those who cheat, taking away people's rights in measure and weight.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويل ﴾ مبتدا خبره ﴿ للمطففين ﴾ للذين يبخسون حقوق الناس فى الكيل والوزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demand complete measure when taking from people; على instead of من indicates that taking from people burdens and disadvantages them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون ﴾ أى إذا أخذوا بالكيل من الناس يأخذون حقوقهم وافية تامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may attach على to يستوفون, putting the object first to restrict their full measure to other people; al-Farrāʾ says من and على alternate here because the debt is owed.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق على يستوفون ويقدم المفعول على الفعل لافادة الاختصاص

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats من and على as interchangeable here: taking from a person means collecting what is owed by that person.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء من وعلى يعتقبان فى هذا الموضع لأنه حق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object pronoun refers to people; the phrasing means they measure or weigh for them, omitting the preposition and making the verb transitive.
rows.anchor: والضمير المنصوب فى ﴿ وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم ﴾ راجع إلى الناس أى كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم فحذف الجار واوصل الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may measure incoming goods because measuring lets them exploit the filling and steal, while weighing allows similar manipulation; when giving out goods they use both measures.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن المطففين كانوا لا يأخذون ما يكال ويوزن إلا بالمكاييل لتمكنهم بالاكتيال من الاستيفاء والسرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yukhsirūn means they reduce what they give; one says that a scale has lost weight or that someone has made it short.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يخسرون ﴾ ينقصون يقال خسر الميزان واخسره

none: The segment repeats the verse's words without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great day is Judgment Day; the interrogative is added to a negation as a rebuke, not as a particle of attention.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ليوم عظيم ﴾ يعنى يوم القيامة ادخل همزة الاستفهام على النافية توبيخا وليست إلا هذه للتنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their audacious cheating is astonishing, as if they never even imagine resurrection and accounting for the smallest amount; if they expected it, they would not short measure.
rows.anchor: وفيه انكار وتعجيب عظيم من حالهم فى الاجتراء على التطفيف كأنهم لا يخطرون ببالهم

rows.speaker: عبد الملك بن مروان
rows.claim: An Arab told ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān that cheaters face the mighty threat he had heard, asking what of a ruler who takes Muslims' wealth without measuring or weighing it.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الملك بن مروان أن اعرابيا قال له لقد سمعت ما قال الله فى المطففين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanūd means intensely ungrateful, especially for the Lord's blessing.
rows.anchor: لكفور أى أنه لنعمة ربه خصوصا لشديد الكفران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A life pleasing in itself may mean one filled with satisfaction or one that is made pleasing to its inhabitant.
rows.anchor: ذات رضا أو مرضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His mother means his dwelling and refuge, with the abode compared to a mother as a child's shelter and recourse.
rows.anchor: فمسكنه ومأواه النار وقيل للمأوى أم على التشبيه لأن الأم مأوى الولد ومفزعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those exempted from loss traded worldly life for the afterlife and so profited and prospered.
rows.anchor: فإنهم اشتروا الآخرة بالدنيا فربحوا وسعدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth means what is firmly established and cannot rightly be denied: all good, including God's oneness, obedience, and following His books and messengers.
rows.anchor: بالأمر الثابت الذى لا يسوغ انكاره وهو الخير كله من توحيد الله وطاعته واتباع كتبه ورسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience means refraining from sins, persisting in obedience, and enduring what God tests His servants with.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وتواصوا بالصبر ﴾ عن المعاصى أو على الطاعات وعلى ما يبلو به الله عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both tawaṣṣaw verbs are past-tense forms coordinated with the preceding past verb.
rows.anchor: وتواصوا فى الموضعين فعل ماض معطوف على ماض قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذي is either an appositive to كل or an accusative of censure.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الذي ﴾ بدل من كل أو نصب على الذم

rows.speaker: شامي
rows.claim: The Syrian, Ḥamza, and ʿAlī reading doubles the verb جمع to emphasize amassing, matching وعدده.
rows.anchor: ﴿ جمع مالا ﴾ جمع شامى وحمزة وعلى مبالغة جمع وهو مطابق لقوله ﴿ وعدده ﴾

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza shares the intensified reading جمع.
rows.anchor: جمع شامى وحمزة وعلى مبالغة جمع

rows.speaker: على
rows.claim: ʿAlī shares the intensified reading جمع.
rows.anchor: جمع شامى وحمزة وعلى مبالغة جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He amassed the wealth and stored it as provision for disasters of the age.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وعدده ﴾ أى جعله عدة لحوادث الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He thinks his wealth will make him immortal in this world, so that he will not die.
rows.anchor: أى تركه خالدا فى الدنيا لا يموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase alludes to righteous deeds as what grant lasting bliss; wealth has made no one immortal.
rows.anchor: أو هو تعريض بالعمل الصالح وأنه هو الذى أخلده صاحبه فى النعيم فأما المال فما أخلد أحدا فيه
